title: FALCON: Force-Adaptive Loco-Manipulation with Feasible Disturbance Curricula
content_lines: Source: [arXiv:2505.06776v2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.06776v2). Code mapping refers to the pinned official FALCON revision linked by the Chinese page.

> **Bottom line:** FALCON separates upper- and lower-body policy objectives while sharing whole-body history, and samples training forces from actuator torque margin through `J^T f`. It improves loaded walking and manipulation robustness, but its sampled-force set is not a real-time safety barrier.
## Engineering problem

Hand forces propagate through the torso and support legs. Independent arm IK and locomotion can fight through the waist, while one monolithic reward can let standing dominate arm accuracy. Uniform random forces also waste training on either trivial or actuator-infeasible disturbances.
## Method

Upper- and lower-body actors have separate rewards/critics but observe shared five-step proprioceptive history; their joint targets are concatenated for whole-body PD. A curriculum maps end-effector force through the Jacobian, subtracts gravity torque, and scales three-axis forces within estimated joint-torque margin.

The hardware table supports one quantified 1.2 kg-per-hand, 0.5 m/s condition; other manipulation demos remain mainly qualitative.
## Decisive evidence

Under strong simulated forces, the dual policy and torque-aware curriculum reduce upper-body error relative to monolithic RL/PID and unconstrained force sampling. Hardware comparison preserves the trade-off with root tracking rather than hiding it in one score.
## Paper-to-implementation mapping

The pinned code exposes maximum end-effector force calculation, force scaling/curriculum, randomized application points, upper-body rewards, and multi-agent PPO configuration. The actual clipped force distribution must be logged, not inferred from nominal bounds.
## Limits and evidence boundary

Axis-wise static torque feasibility omits joint coupling, impact, friction cones, thermal limits, and contact-task objectives. Actors infer force through history rather than direct sensing, so onset and sustained-contact behavior need separate tests. Quantitative hardware evidence is narrow.
## Bounded engineering takeaway

Generate disturbances from actuator opportunity rather than arbitrary magnitude, and compare decomposition against parameter-matched unified and no-shared-history baselines. Keep force adaptation separate from the task's required contact-force controller.
## Reproduction checklist

Lock Jacobians, gravity torque, limits, force sampler, application point, filters, curriculum, actor observations, action merge, PD, and randomization. Report arm error, root error, foot slip, saturation, impact, temperature, falls, and recovery for force onset, steady force, and release.
